name: hushbox
//devEngines: The Node runtime is declared here and resolved into `pnpm-lock.yaml`, so the exact version is a resolution the consuming tool produced rather than a second copy anything keeps aligned. It replaces an `engines.node` field, which is not to be restored beside it: `engines.node` makes pnpm warn once per install-class invocation whenever the shell Node differs from the range, and `pnpm dev` reaches install through `ensure-stack`. Editing the range without re-resolving fails a `--frozen-lockfile` install with ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE, so the two cannot drift apart silently.
//arch:scan: The heap ceiling on the arch:scan script is not a rule-set cost: the rules share one ts-morph project over the whole declared scope, the sources the globs select plus the declaration files their imports reach, so nothing is loaded per rule and the floor is the tree. Measured at this ceiling the run peaks near 5 GB resident, which has to fit the runner the gate's CI job takes (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`). The number sits on the gate's own script line rather than in the environment so that every route to the gate carries it, CI included, with nothing to set and nothing to remember. Raising it defers rather than fixes: what exhausts it is the tree growing, and there is little room above it before that runner's own memory binds.

//devDependencies: `css-select`, `css-tree`, `domutils` and `htmlparser2` are declared here for a consumer outside every workspace: the frontend-design skill's static-HTML detector (`.claude/skills/frontend-design/scripts/detector/engines/static-html/detect-html.mjs`) imports all four as bare specifiers from a directory no workspace glob matches, so the symlinks a root declaration creates in the root `node_modules` are the only resolution path it has. Those imports sit in a `try`/`catch` that falls back to a regex-only scan, so dropping a declaration costs the parsed-HTML path silently. Collapsing the tree onto one major is the `overrides` block in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, not these declarations; neither substitutes for the other.
